requirements.text: create a new application service named User App, that is going to be used in production, marked as operational, and treated as a critical service ... owned by Priya and its description should briefly capture its role as the primary interface through which users authenticate and access core business functionality
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service WHERE service_id = 'SVC_005' AND name = 'User App' AND owned_by = 'USER_002' AND used_for = 'production' AND status = 'operational' AND service_classification = 'application' AND business_criticality = 'critical' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%primary%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%authenticat%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%access%' AND LOWER(description) LIKE '%function%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (SVC_005 after SVC_004); the only service the task creates; the benchmark's problem check also expects SVC_005
owner is Priya, resolved to USER_002 (Priya Sharma), the only Priya in the seed
'application service' read as service_classification = application, an existing value in the seed (SVC_004)
used_for production, status operational and business_criticality critical are the seed's spellings of the request's words
the description's wording is free-form; the four LIKE stems are kept from the benchmark check and match the request's own words (primary interface, authenticate, access, functionality)

disagreement: sql form: A writes description LIKE ..., B wraps it in LOWER() as the benchmark does; chose B's form because sql keeps the benchmark check's own form of the count query, which applies LOWER(); SQLite's LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII, so the cells read the same either way
org_id is not fixed by the request ('for the organization') or the benchmark check and is not tested; the acting user and Priya are both in ORG_001

requirements.text: A new problem now needs to be logged in connection with this service ... identified on the item located in the country of United States of America with a cost lower than 1000, where user authentication is fully blocked and no operational work can continue until restoration is achieved ... the highest available levels of impact, urgency, and priority
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE problem_id = 'PRB_003' AND service = 'SVC_005' AND configuration_item = 'CI_002' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND status = 'new' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%block%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%restorat%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%authenticat%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%work%' AND LOWER(problem_statement) LIKE '%achieve%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (PRB_003 after PRB_002); the only problem the task creates
'in connection with this service' read as service = SVC_005, the service the first requirement creates

the item is CI_002 (Aisha Desktop, LOC_001 New York, cost 800): the only CI at a location whose country is USA with cost below 1000; the seed spells the country 'USA', taken as the United States of America
highest available levels: impact high and urgency high are the policy's highest enumerated values; priority critical is both the highest level and the policy's problem matrix value for (high, high)
status new: the policy's default for new problems; kept from the benchmark check
the problem statement's wording is free-form; the five LIKE stems are kept from the benchmark check and match the request's words (blocked, restoration, authentication, work, achieved)
disagreement: sql form: A writes problem_statement LIKE ..., B wraps it in LOWER() as the benchmark does; chose B's form for the reason given on the service requirement
opened_by, category, org_id, original_task and short_description are not fixed by the request or the benchmark check and are not cells; CI_002 is in_use so policy 5.1 allows the link

requirements.text: the item located in the country of United States of America with a cost lower than 1000
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM problem WHERE configuration_item IN ('CI_001', 'CI_003', 'CI_004')
assumptions: boundary of the CI selector: the other three CIs are also at USA locations but cost 1200, 1500 and 6000, so a reading that keeps the country and drops the cost bound (CI_001 at 1200 is the nearest) must not link them to any problem; no problem links them on the seed

disagreement: B only; kept because the request picks the CI by description, not by id, and these three are exactly the rows a loose reading of that description (country kept, cost bound dropped) would sweep in; a second problem opened on one of them would pass the anchored create requirement without this stay

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the two created rows (service SVC_005 owned by Priya, problem PRB_003 on SVC_005 and CI_002 at the highest levels), on every cell value and on both dispositions (kept). disagreement: boundary stay on problem.configuration_item for CI_001, CI_003 and CI_004 (B only; A wrote no stay, reading the CI description as unambiguous); kept because all four CIs sit at USA locations and only the cost bound separates CI_002, so a loose reading sweeps in the other three, which makes them the boundary of the CI description; it is zero on the seed and adds strictness only where a problem is opened on a CI outside the description. disagreement: sql form on the two LIKE cells: A drops the benchmark's LOWER(), B keeps it; chose B's form because sql keeps the benchmark checks' own form of the count query, which applies LOWER(), and the cell predicates are identical in both passes (logged on each requirement). The requirement texts are A's shorter quotations; B quoted the sentences in full, with the same meaning. Both passes leave the problem's category open (the request names none and the policy fixes none) and agree policy 4.2's incident-linking rule adds nothing, as the request names no incident. revised: the boundary stay's reason, on the requirement and in these notes, now states itself (the three other USA CIs are what a reading without the cost bound would pick) instead of citing an outside rule. revised: the LOWER() disagreement's reason, on the service requirement and in these notes, now states itself (sql follows the benchmark checks' own form) instead of citing an outside document.
